content:
sasha: heads up — ran a 2-node 8xA100 multi-GPU profile this morning, and tail latency for short-chat workloads jumped ~2.8x after the kernel-selector change.
sasha: brief summary: small sequence lengths (<=64), lots of tiny all-reduces, KV cache hitrate is fine but we see long stalls right before token emit.
sasha: annotated perf trace attached to the run in CI (link: https://ci.redwood/recipes/run/4892) — TL;DR: comm stalls dominate, NCCL shows LL128 channels enabled by default on that cluster.

devon: can you paste the profiler snippet? curious about comm/compute overlap numbers
sasha: sure — here's a trimmed perf-lite dump from bench-run 4892:

```
ProfilerSummary:
  total_tokens: 1.2M
  avg_latency_token_ms: 18.5 -> (tail 99p: 42)
  compute_time_pct: 28
  comm_wait_pct: 64
  kvcache_lookup_ms: 0.9
  pipeline_idle_pct: 12
```

liam: whoa comm_wait 64% is too high for these small messages. any sign of allreduce fragmentation? message sizes?
sasha: small messages ~3-20KB per tensor allreduce (per step), many tiny collectives interleaved with compute, and NCCL logs show frequent LL128 channel contention.

benchbot: infra note — cluster config: driver 520.xx, NCCL 2.17, CUDA 11.8, kernel-selector v2.3.1 (rolled yesterday)

devon: hypothesis: kernel-selector now chooses a fused attention kernel that increases time in compute but reduces compute concurrency windows, which exposes more frequent, smaller NCCL ops -> channels starving/serialize and LL128 small-msg penalty.

liam: I remember LL vs LL128 tradeoff: LL128 sometimes wins for larger msgs or pipelined flows, but for tiny allreduces LL (or SIMPLE) + fewer channels can be better. maybe kernel-selector assumed larger batch sizes and flipped algo.

renee: can we repro quickly with toggles? suggestion: run the same trace with env overrides: `NCCL_PROTO=LL` and `NCCL_ALGO=RING` and also `NCCL_MAX_NRINGS=1` (if available) to force fewer channels. also try `NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD` lower/raise depending on build.

sasha: starting a repro matrix now. patching bench job to run 3 variants: (A) default (LL128+auto), (B) NCCL_PROTO=LL, (C) NCCL_ALGO=RING + NCCL_MAX_NRINGS=1. will post numbers.

infra-bot: job 4892-repro-a queued on pool-8 (ETA ~12m)

(devon edits) devon: another angle — KV cache behavior: kernel-selector changed fused-kernel ordering which increased prefetch misses ~4%. that increases short-lived compute, leading to more scatter/gather on comm side.

liam: if prefetch misses increased, that increases the # of KV-aware token paths which may cause more tiny gradients/keys to be exchanged? can you share the kvcache hit logs?
sasha: snippet:
```
KVCacheStats:
  lookups: 1,203,445
  hits: 1,157,200 (96.2%)
  misses: 46,245
  avg_miss_latency_ms: 1.6
```
liam: not huge misses but the misses are bursty — bursts align with channel saturation windows in the trace.

renee: interim mitigation: add a runtime probe that measures per-request comm_msg_size distribution and if median_msg_size < 16KB switch kernel-selector to favor compute-parallel schedule that groups small collectives, or temporarily switch NCCL to LL mode for that deployment.

devon: +1 to a dynamic probe. we can add a keep-alive micro-batcher that coalesces short allreduces into a single larger collective when latency SLO permits.

sasha: repro results (quick numbers):
- default: 99p token latency 42ms, comm_wait 64%
- NCCL_PROTO=LL: 99p 29ms, comm_wait 42%
- RING + 1 ring: 99p 31ms, comm_wait 45%

sasha: summary: forcing LL (no LL128 channels) improved tail latency a lot for this workload.

liam: interesting — so LL128 channelization was hurting small-msg throughput here. this matches our theory: LL128 adds more channels and increases serialization overhead for many tiny ops.

renee: action items:
- renée: file a short postmortem + perf experiment in eng-runtime about this regression and mark kernel-selector v2.3.1 as suspect (I'll own).
- liam: prototype a runtime probe to detect median comm_msg_size and flip NCCL env heuristics dynamically (opt-in with feature flag).
- devon: add a micro-batcher toggle in the serving runtime to fold concurrent tiny allreduces within a time window.
- sasha: re-run full ci suite on the cluster with LL forced and confirm no regressions on large-batch workloads.

sasha: tagging @liam @renee @devon — I'll attach full flamegraphs once the repro run finishes.

benchbot: job 4892-repro-(B) completed: artifacts uploaded to s3://perf-runs/4892-B

devon: thanks — once we have flamegraphs I'll open a PR to kernel-selector to add a new cost-model term for comm_imbalance_penalty. if we can quantify the penalty per-msg-size and #channels we can make an automatic decision.

liam: one more note — check NCCL versions. upstream NCCL added fixes for LL128 scheduling in 2.18; we should test with newer NCCL too. but runtime-level probes are safer short-term.

renee: agreed. filing follow-ups in triage board. :white_check_mark:

sasha: thanks all, closing for now — will update when large-batch runs finish.
